entry.title: Apple Creator Studio update: MotionVFX and AI
entry.summary: 3 minute read Apple Creator Studio update: MotionVFX and AI 5:36 Apple Creator Studio's November update, free to existing subscribers, puts MotionVFX inside Final Cut Pro. Logic Pro, Keynote, Pages, and Numbers gain beta AI assistants. While everyone was primed for Apple hardware
entry.content:
3 minute read
Apple Creator Studio update: MotionVFX and AI
5:36

Apple Creator Studio's November update, free to existing subscribers, puts MotionVFX inside Final Cut Pro. Logic Pro, Keynote, Pages, and Numbers gain beta AI assistants.

While everyone was primed for Apple hardware releases today, much more unexpected was a new version of Apple Creator Studio for Mac, iPad, and iPhone. Apple’s creative apps used to be updated with fairly glacial slowness, but Apple seems to have kicked things up a gear now that it has Creator Studio subscriptions to sell. Creator Studio only went on sale in January this year, and this will be the fourth update to hit the App Store.

Final Cut Pro gets supercharged

Final Cut Pro for Mac probably gets the biggest update across the range, and now includes built-in MotionVFX, following Apple’s purchase of the company back in March. This adds thousands of elements, including effects, plug-ins, transitions, templates, titles, graphics, and tools for rotoscoping, tracking, and color grading. Also, any image on the timeline can now be opened in Pixelmator Pro and saved back to the project automatically.

Apple is less front and center with AI tools than some rivals, but all the same, Final Cut Pro adds AI image generation from text descriptions. Elsewhere it gets more keyframe easing options, the ability to disconnect clips from the primary storyline and place them anywhere on the timeline, and 23 new transcription languages.

The Content Hub, an Apple-curated library of stock videos, photos, and backgrounds, now includes video assets and is available in Final Cut Pro. No word yet on its size, but it’s interesting to see Cupertino expand on what it contains.

Motion and Pixelmator Pro

In the wider app portfolio, Motion adds built-in MotionVFX plug-ins for color grading, 3D camera tracking, and one-click selection, plus image generation from text descriptions, round-tripping to Pixelmator Pro, keyframe easing, a Displacement filter, and an interactive demo project. Compressor can encode Cinematic mode video recorded on iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo.

Pixelmator Pro itself unsurprisingly adds Generate Fill, which realistically sees it playing catch-up with rival image editing software. This edits a user-selected area from a text description, matching lighting, perspective, and the texture of the surrounding area. Built-in Super Resolution upscales the generated content. Generated elements can be merged into existing layers or inserted as new layers with masking.

Logic Pro updates

Logic Pro for Mac and iPad gets a Liquid Glass design, while Logic Pro for Mac adds an assistant in beta, powered by Apple-built models and OpenAI, for navigating production workflows, starting a song, setting up a vocal track from a single prompt, or refining a project. It also gets a redesigned Browser covering loops, instruments, effect patches, and a Splice library.

Music understanding, an on-device audio analysis tool, classifies and tags added sounds, so users can search the whole collection or drag in a loop to find matching audio, which should save time wading through libraries of sounds. Stem Splitter can also now isolate, replace, or rebalance drum parts without the original multitracks. A new Producer Pack from Sergio George includes his piano sound and Latin jazz and salsa loops, including percussion, brass, and basses. Voice Memo Studio Sound reduces room ambience and background noise in recordings from supported iPhone models, with the option to continue in Logic Pro.

Productivity? Sweet...

And the more controversial members of the Creator Studio offering, the everyday productivity apps of Keynote, Pages, and Numbers, also get new features. This starts with an assistant in beta, built on Apple models and OpenAI, that understands document context. In Keynote it helps design, animate, and refine slides; in Pages it drafts, restructures, and fine-tunes text; and in Numbers it calculates, visualizes, and organizes data, recommends chart types with a one-tap preview, and builds custom tables using world knowledge.

Model Context Protocol (MCP) support lets external AI agents and tools read content, perform edits, and run automated actions. The Content Hub in Keynote, Pages, and Numbers adds stock video, and there are new templates and themes. Keynote adds support for Keynote Interchange Format (.keyx), an open JSON-based bundle format. Freeform adds text styles for formatting and reuse across boards, plus custom and preset board background colors. In December it will add image editing in Pixelmator Pro and generation of editable shapes from text.

Pricing and availability

The update arrives on the App Store in November, free for existing subscribers. In the US, new subscribers pay $12.99 per month or $129 per year, with a one-month free trial. Customers who buy a new Mac or qualifying iPad can receive three months free. Education pricing for college students and educators is $2.99 per month or $29.99 per year. Creator Studio is a universal purchase, and up to six family members can share it with Family Sharing. One-time purchases on the Mac App Store are Final Cut Pro ($299), Logic Pro ($199), Pixelmator Pro ($49.99), Motion ($49.99), Compressor ($49.99), and MainStage ($29.99). Free versions of Keynote, Pages, Numbers, and Freeform remain available and come with every new iPhone, Mac, and iPad.

entry.summary: 2 minute read M6 iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro: specs and prices 4:34 Apple has announced two new computers, the 24-inch iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro, both built around the M6 chip. Prices start from $1499 and $1999. And still we wait for tomorrow and the official announcement of
entry.content:
2 minute read
M6 iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro: specs and prices
4:34

Apple has announced two new computers, the 24-inch iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro, both built around the M6 chip. Prices start from $1499 and $1999. And still we wait for tomorrow and the official announcement of the touchscreen MacBooks.

24-inch M6 iMac

We’ll start with the new 24-inch iMac with M6. It comes with a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU, or up to a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, each two more cores than before. The GPU has Neural Accelerators in each core, and there is a Dual 16-core Neural Engine. Memory bandwidth is up to 170 GB/s.

Apple loves its benchmarks and says that the GPU delivers up to 2x faster graphics than M4, the Neural Engine up to 2x faster AI compute than the previous generation, on-device AI up to 5x faster than M4, and SSD read and write up to 2x faster.

For Intel-based upgraders (if there are any left out there), Apple quotes up to 18x faster performance than the most popular Intel-based iMac.

The 4.5K Retina display has an actual diagonal of 23.5 inches, 500 nits of brightness, and P3 wide color covering over 1 billion colors. Apple says it has 5x more resolution and nearly 70% greater brightness than the bestselling 24-inch all-in-one PC, but that’s enough of a limited category it doesn’t feel like a particularly valid comparison. A nano-texture option is available on the more expensive 12-core models.

Connectivity is WiFi 7 and Bluetooth 6, with optional 2.5 Gb Ethernet (up to 2.5x faster wired than the previous generation) and up to four Thunderbolt 4 ports on 12-core models. It supports up to two 6K external displays. There is a 12 MP Center Stage camera with Desk View, two pairs of force-cancelling woofers with two tweeters, Spatial Audio with Dolby Atmos support, and a three-microphone array.

The iMac comes in seven colors: blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange, and silver. It includes a color-matched keyboard and mouse or trackpad with USB-C ports. Touch ID is standard on 12-core models, while 10-core models can be configured with Magic Keyboard with Touch ID and Numeric Keypad.

Pricing and availability

Pre-orders open October 28 in 35 countries and regions, with availability from Friday, November 6. The 10-core model starts at $1499. The 12-core model starts at $1699. Apple Upgrade leasing starts at $28.99 per month for 36 months, excluding taxes and trade-in credit.

14-inch MacBook Pro with M6

The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 also raises the bar over its predecessors to an impressive degree. The chip has a 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU with a Neural Accelerator in each core, and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine; the CPU and GPU each have two more cores than before. Memory is 16 GB unified as standard, configurable up to 32 GB, with bandwidth up to 170 GB/s. Apple says the GPU is up to 30% faster for graphics and up to 25% faster for AI workloads than M5, and that the Neural Engine is up to 1.9x faster than M5.

One more benchmark comparison is well worth noting: battery life is up to 24 hours, which is up to 14 hours more for Intel-based upgraders and up to four hours more for M1 users. It’s also the same as with the M5 model.

The Liquid Retina XDR display reaches up to 1600 nits peak HDR brightness with a 1,000,000:1 contrast ratio, and a nano-texture option is available. Connectivity includes WiFi 7, Bluetooth 6, support for up to two external displays, HDMI, MagSafe 3, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, an SDXC card slot, and a headphone jack.

There is also a 12 MP Center Stage camera with Desk View, a three-mic array, and a six-speaker system with Spatial Audio.

Fast charging reaches up to 50% in 30 minutes with a compatible higher-wattage USB-C adapter such as the 96 W Power Adapter.

Pricing and availability

It comes in space black and silver. Pre-orders open October 28 in 35 countries and regions, with availability from Friday, November 6. Pricing starts at $1999. Apple Upgrade leasing starts at $38.99 per month for 36 months, excluding taxes and trade-in credit.

entry.content:
2 minute read
DaVinci Resolve 21.1.2: new features and fixes
3:07

Blackmagic has improved timeline edit point selection and made OGraf playback up to 4x faster in DaVinci Resolve 21.1.2. Studio also speeds up IntelliSearch on Apple M6.

Blackmagic has released DaVinci Resolve 21.1.2 and Fusion Studio 21.1.2, following the major 21.1 release in September and 21.1.1 earlier this month.

DaVinci Resolve 21.1.2 adds improved timeline edit point selection, as well as up to 4x faster OGraf playback, additional template controls, and support for OGraf and Lottie graphics on Linux. The OGraf changes are also in Fusion Studio 21.1.2, which adds custom clip input and output labels for OpenFX.

DaVinci Resolve Studio 21.1.2 adds IntelliSearch analysis that Blackmagic says is up to 14x faster on Apple M6 computers running macOS 27.IntelliSearch analysis, multicam SmartSwitch, and other AI tools run faster on Intel graphics platforms, while Magic Mask caches use less disk space, and there are multiple scripting API improvements. The software is currently 20% off until November 20.

As usual, all updates are free and available from the Blackmagic support page. Here are the full changelogs of new or updated features.

What's new in DaVinci Resolve 21.1.2

The following features have been added or updated.

  • Select nearest edit point type prioritizes selected edit points.
  • Lasso selecting edit points can now enter dynamic trim automatically.
  • Selecting edit points for gaps now activates trim editor.
  • Timeline view option to display current clip indicator.
  • Option to show loudness meters in the edit mixer.
  • Project settings option to disable DNG lens correction.
  • OGraf clips now use action durations to place stop actions.
  • Up to 4x faster OGraf playback in edit and Fusion pages.
  • Support for OGraf select and multi-select template controls.
  • OGraf responsive templates now adapt to timeline aspect ratio.
  • Support for OGraf and Lottie graphics on Linux.
  • Improved HDR global wheel trackball sensitivity on color panels.
  • Fast Noise option to follow the FX tracker.
  • Addressed double squeezed anamorphic video output in Fusion.
  • Addressed issue with Follower animation using expressions.
  • Addressed overlay issues with SDI and remote monitoring.
  • Addressed issue with searches in a smart bin.
  • Addressed empty folder in user directory when loading DRP files.
  • Addressed issue with selecting multiple titles and subtitles.
  • Addressed timeline in-out range issues in collaboration projects.
  • Addressed Quick Export not using selected trim pass grade.
  • Addressed issue with geometry thumbnails in the media pool.
  • Addressed Recent 5 Mins mode inserting full clips.
  • Addressed loudness meter not resetting after Cut page scrubbing.
  • General performance and stability improvements.

In addition to the above, Resolve Studio 21.1.2 adds the following:

  • Up to 14x faster IntelliSearch analysis on M6 with macOS 27.
  • Improved AI tool performance on Intel platforms.
  • Improved disk space usage for Magic Mask caches.
  • Multiple scripting API improvements.
  • Addressed issue with Film Look Creator gate weave controls.
  • Addressed HDR Vivid metadata issues in imported CPL timelines.
  • Addressed Speech Generator disk usage and speed on macOS 27.
  • Addressed issues with Music Remixer on macOS 27.
  • Addressed render failures for in-out ranges with Magic Mask clips.
  • General performance and stability improvements.

What's new in Fusion Studio 21.1.2

The following features have been added or updated.

  • Addressed issue with channel names in Displace 3D.
  • Addressed issue with running some Lua scripts.
  • Addressed memory issue with some Perspective Positioner settings.
  • Addressed issue with Mapped Duplicate 3D time mapping inputs.
  • Addressed issue with selecting multiple titles clearing text.
  • Addressed issue with dropdown controls not always creating undo events.
  • Addressed issue with Follower animation using expressions.
  • Addressed issue with very small erode dilate levels.
  • Addressed issue with Film Look Creator gate weave controls.
  • Addressed issue with some scripts on ARM64 systems.
  • Addressed issue with slow reading of large EXR headers.
  • Addressed issue with OGraf custom text field sizes.
  • Support OGraf dropdown choice parameters.
  • Support OGraf rendering on Linux.
  • Improved OGraf inspector action controls.
  • General performance and stability improvements.

entry.content:
2 minute read
instax mini Evo 2: price, specs, release date
3:29

The instax mini Evo 2 adds a 4.5-inch touchscreen, a larger sensor, and a wider 21mm lens. It arrives in late November at $289.

With its instax line allowing Fujifilm to make money hand over fist at the moment, the company has announced the instax mini Evo 2 hybrid instant camera, along with an updated instax mini Evo smartphone app.

There are some decent upgrades to the now $289 camera with the built-in printer that has been such an Insta crowd pleaser since the original was first released in 2021. The extra $90 over the original’s $199 launch price will perhaps temper some of the enthusiasm (that is a hefty 45% price rise), but you can argue that the new features are strong enough that they justify it.

Larger screen and Immersive Movie

The mini Evo 2 has a larger 1/2.77-inch sensor, and its lens is now a 21mm equivalent f/2.0, against 28mm on the original. The extra hardware adds bulk, at 330 g (11.6 oz) against 285 g (10.1 oz), and 87.5 x 125.3 x 43.7 mm (3.4 x 4.9 x 1.7 in) against 87 x 122.9 x 36 mm (3.4 x 4.8 x 1.4 in).

That, though, allows it to accommodate a new 4.5-inch LCD 1.23 million dot touchscreen. This is a significant upgrade on the 3.0-inch 460,000 dot screen of the original, and allows the company to offer a new feature called Expanded View. This provides a wider field of view than the 46 x 62 mm shooting area, with an on-screen framing guide also included to help in composition.

The Evo 2 prints in about 14 seconds (a faster print than the original’s roughly 16 secs), and gets about 90 prints per charge, down from 100. The camera holds about 45 shots in internal memory. Still resolution is 2144 x 2860 (6.1 MP), or 3100 x 4128 (12.8 MP) with microSD and Expanded View off.

There is also a new instax Immersive Movie feature that follows on from the tech developed for the instax mini Evo Cinema. The Evo Cinema provides 15 seconds per clip, while the mini Evo 2 records four seconds of 560 x 992 MP4 video at 24 fps leading up to each photo. This requires a microSD card. The camera can’t record movies to internal memory.

If it ain't broke...

Elsewhere, many of the features are carried over from the original in a "if it ain’t broke, don’t fix it" manner. The mini Evo 2 offers 10x lens effects and 10x film effects, for what the company rather cutely calculates as 100 ways to customize content, plus what it calls analog-inspired controls. It also has adjustable exposure, white balance, and flash, a macro mode, and a built-in selfie mirror.

Print resolution is 600 dpi, with a choice of instax-Rich Mode or instax-Natural Mode. There is a microSD slot and USB Type-C charging.

Smartphone printing and remote shooting use the free instax mini Evo app, and the camera prints 2" x 3" instax mini instant photos, with film sold separately.

Pricing and availability

The instax Evo 2 is expected at the end of November 2026 with a suggested retail price of $289.

entry.summary: 2 minute read Apple iPad mini A20 Pro: specs, price, release 3:41 Apple has announced the OLED iPad mini with an A20 Pro chip and IP67 rating. It starts at $699 and arrives November 6. Earlier today, the first signs arrived that Apple would announce its new touchscreen MacBooks a
entry.content:
2 minute read
Apple iPad mini A20 Pro: specs, price, release
3:41

Apple has announced the OLED iPad mini with an A20 Pro chip and IP67 rating. It starts at $699 and arrives November 6.

Earlier today, the first signs arrived that Apple would announce its new touchscreen MacBooks and more as a series of daily reveals leading up to Wednesday's touchscreen MacBook announcement. And so it has proved, with Monday being the day earmarked for news of a new iPad mini.

With availability starting Friday, November 6, it gets a decent spec bump over the previous generation released in 2024. It also gets an unfortunate price bump too, coming in at a starting price of $699, $200 more than before (though it has been raised to $599 since).

Weight loss program

It is both thinner and lighter than the 2024 model. It weighs 255 g (0.56 lb) in WiFi form and 263 g (0.58 lb) with cellular, down from 293 g (0.65 lb) and 297 g (0.66 lb) on the 2024 model. It is also 0.9 mm (0.04 in) thinner at 5.4 mm (0.21 in) against 6.3 mm (0.25 in), a cut of roughly 14%. Height is essentially unchanged at 195.3 mm (7.69 in), but width drops 2.2 mm (0.09 in) to 132.6 mm (5.22 in).

It is based around an 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR OLED display, up from 8.3-inch, which (mostly) keeps the previous mini’s footprint thanks to 24% thinner bezels. It supports the P3 wide color gamut, with peak brightness up to 1200 nits (more than 2x the previous generation), 600 nits full-screen for SDR and HDR, a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio, and a 1-nit minimum brightness. A nano-texture option is available for the 256 and 512 GB models.

It’s powered by the latest A20 Pro chip built on a 2 nm process and has a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each core and up to a 6-core CPU. Apple claims up to 4.5x faster AI performance, up to 2.7x faster graphics, and up to 60% faster multithreaded CPU performance than the previous generation, plus more than 2x the unified memory bandwidth.

The 512 GB configuration adds a Dual 16-core Neural Engine.

New Acoustic Display

Alongside the very welcome presence of IP67 water and dust resistance, probably its biggest innovation rather than iteration comes with the new Acoustic Display. This pairs woofers through the display with custom tweeters located between the glass and aluminum enclosure. It will be interesting to see how this performs, with the first feedback likely from the Pro and tell event on Wednesday, as such designs can lack bottom end and stereo width, especially at the iPad mini scale.

Elsewhere, the 12 MP Center Stage front camera moves to the landscape edge, while the 12 MP Wide back camera supports Smart HDR 4 and 4K video at up to 60 fps, and gains an Adaptive True Tone flash. The new Apple N1 chip provides WiFi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. Cellular models use the C2 modem, with up to 50% faster data speeds than the previous generation, and support eSIM. Fast-charge is also supported.

Pricing and availability

US pricing starts at $699 for WiFi and $849 for WiFi + Cellular, in 128 GB, 256 GB, and 512 GB configurations. Pre-orders open Wednesday, October 28 in 36 countries and regions.

entry.title: iPhone Duo screen cracks: what iFixit found
entry.summary: 2 minute read iPhone Duo screen cracks: what iFixit found 3:09 iFixit's teardown suggests the iPhone Duo's hinge center support bar may be behind its cracked inner screens. Apple is reportedly replacing affected phones. iFixit has torn down the iPhone Duo and given it a provision
entry.content:
2 minute read
iPhone Duo screen cracks: what iFixit found
3:09

iFixit's teardown suggests the iPhone Duo's hinge center support bar may be behind its cracked inner screens. Apple is reportedly replacing affected phones.

iFixit has torn down the iPhone Duo and given it a provisional 5/10 repairability score. That might not seem great, but it is the highest score it has awarded a foldable to date, which tells you a lot about the complexity of these devices. And it is partly that complexity that seems to be leading to multiple reports of cracked screens from around the world.

First off, let’s look at what iFixit found. The inner display has a matte nano-texture finish that scatters reflections in an attempt to hide the crease. With it removed, the crease looks arguably more visible than on, say, the Galaxy Z Fold8. Looking at the area under a microscope reveals that some subpixels are oval and point in different directions. iFixit points to an Apple patent application on reducing diffraction artifacts as a possible explanation.

 

 

The nano-texture finish sits on a replaceable polymer cover. Replacing it costs $49 ($19 with AppleCare+) at an Apple Store, while replacing the inner display costs $999 without coverage, half the price of a new device.

The hinge itself uses metal joints, springs, and synchronization gears around a teardrop-shaped curve, so the closed screen follows a gentle curve inside the hinge. If that sounds simple, it’s actually not, as the display’s layers also need to slide against each other while it curves round.

Cracking on

So, what’s causing the cracks? To find out, iFixit built a 3D model of the hinge based on a combination of teardown footage, patents, and CT scans. It then compared this with the reported damage locations, which mostly follow the same pattern: a thin line along the fold and a brighter, thicker line extending horizontally across the right-hand side of the screen just below the halfway point. Users also report hearing a loud pop just before the screen breaks.

iFixit’s model places the breaks slightly below the cable’s path through the hinge, and its simulation shows that the center support bar can fail to drop far enough to accommodate the folded screen. This would create a stress hotspot near where the breaks have been reported.

It’s worth pointing out at the moment that this is a hypothesis, but iFixit’s testing and stellar track record in this area show that it’s a reasonable one. The question is, what happens next? Is this a small manufacturing defect affecting a tiny sample of new iPhone Duos, or a larger problem that will eventually affect most units? Given the extensive testing that the Duo went through you have to hope the former, but we’ve already seen some high-profile devices such as the Sony FX5 hit problems that you think would have been caught before release, so you never know.

Apple has yet to officially respond to what online wags are calling Crackgate, but so far reports are that Apple is replacing affected devices wholesale rather than trying to implement repairs.

entry.title: CIPA August 2026: camera and lens shipments
entry.summary: 2 minute read CIPA August 2026: camera and lens shipments 3:10 CIPA data shows camera makers shipped 3.2% fewer cameras from January to August, but shipped value rose 3.7% as prices rise. Full-frame fell almost 20% while compacts grew 15%. Japanese camera industry trade body CIPA
entry.content:
2 minute read
CIPA August 2026: camera and lens shipments
3:10

CIPA data shows camera makers shipped 3.2% fewer cameras from January to August, but shipped value rose 3.7% as prices rise. Full-frame fell almost 20% while compacts grew 15%.

Japanese camera industry trade body CIPA’s (Camera & Imaging Products Association) latest data has just been published, and the news from August 2026 is decidedly mixed. On the one hand, between January and August this year, member companies shipped 5.7 million digital cameras worldwide, 3.2% fewer than in the same period of 2025. On the other, the shipped value of all those cameras rose 3.7% to about ¥572 billion ($3.65 billion).

A weakness in the market for interchangeable-lens cameras (ILCs) accounts for the drop. Shipments of 4.01 million bodies were 9.3% down, yet their value rose 1.5% to about ¥465 billion ($2.97 billion). Mirrorless cameras, which make up 92% of ILC units, fell 6.2% to 3.7 million while value rose 3.4%.

By our calculations, that works out at roughly ¥122,000 ($778) shipped value per mirrorless body, about 10% more than a year ago.

Wider rumors of a resurgence in DSLRs seem wide of the mark, however. These fell 35% in terms of units and 37% in terms of value, and now make up under 8% of ILC shipments. Effectively, they’re a niche product nowadays.

There is a definite division along the lines of ILC sensor size. Cameras with 35mm or larger sensors fell 19.8% in units and 6.5% in value, while smaller-sensor models dipped 3.2% in units and gained 14% in value.

So, where is the growth coming from? Fixed-lens cameras basically, up 15.3% to 1.69 million units and 14.1% in value, which reached about ¥107 billion ($0.68 billion). They now make up almost 30% of everything CIPA members ship, and in August alone they were up almost a third on the year.

It’s worth pointing out that lenses are still holding up better compared to bodies. Shipments of 6.31 million lenses were 4.9% lower, but value rose 4.4% to about ¥340 billion ($2.17 billion), and the lens-to-body ratio stands at 1.57, up from 1.50 a year ago, i.e. 1.57 lenses are shipped for every camera body.

Regionally, China (down 20.8%), the Americas (down 12.9%), and Europe (down 10.9%) were shipped fewer ILCs, while Asia outside Japan and China rose 12.3%, and Japan 6.7%.

CIPA’s February forecast of 6.82 million ILC bodies for the year now looks out of reach, as it would require monthly shipments about 40% above the year-to-date average. The comparison also flatters the 2026 figures, because CIPA added Kenko Tokina to its camera statistics from January and has not adjusted year-on-year figures. That means any like-for-like declines are probably steeper than reported.

entry.title: Adobe BWT Alpine F1 partnership: AI fan experience
entry.summary: 2 minute read Adobe BWT Alpine F1 partnership: AI fan experience 2:34 Adobe will become BWT Alpine Formula One Team's Official AI Fan Experience Partner next season in a deal that covers content creation, fan data, AI search visibility, and design tools. We’ve already written abo
entry.content:
2 minute read
Adobe BWT Alpine F1 partnership: AI fan experience
2:34

Adobe will become BWT Alpine Formula One Team's Official AI Fan Experience Partner next season in a deal that covers content creation, fan data, AI search visibility, and design tools.

We’ve already written about F1 once this week. Now comes a second chance for us to blather on about bargeboards and tire strategies as Adobe and the BWT Alpine Formula One Team have announced a global premium partnership.

So far, this is less about Adobe Creative Cloud products being used in the Alpine marketing efforts, and more about Adobe becoming the Official AI Fan Experience Partner for the team. It’s going to be a bigger deal than it first appears, though. The partnership applies from the 2027 Formula One season and beyond, and next season the team’s main title sponsor becomes Gucci. That means the team name changes to the Gucci Racing Alpine Formula One Team, and you can expect its profile to start ramping up from there.

The partnership to date covers four initiatives. Adobe GenStudio, an AI-powered content production tool, will be used to create personalized content variations for fans. Adobe Experience Platform will give the team a real-time view of fan engagement, used to choose messages and channels, while Adobe Brand Visibility, an AI search optimization system, will show how the team appears across AI agents and LLMs. And finally Adobe Express will let the team offer fans design tools with generative AI image generation.

If all that covers a whole load of tools you are unfamiliar with, then likewise. But it does give an insight into how AI is inveigling its way into all areas of a major branding effort like those you associate with F1 teams. We’re sure it won’t be too long before we can start talking about things we’re more familiar with when it comes to the team’s activities.

And, as its 2027 driver line up announcement shows, Alpine has definitely got game.

The team is firmly in the midpack when it comes to F1. But even if it hasn’t made the jump up to the Big Four of Mercedes, Ferrari, McLaren, and Red Bull as yet this season, despite some promising results for French driver Pierre Gasly, leveling up its off-track activities is an important part of the F1 marketing mix. And the new Gucci branding is going to take it stratospheric.

Those that somewhat despair of encroaching ‘sleb culture on the grid might want to look away now. Which is funnily enough just what the TV director tends to do, normally when something interesting is going on on the racetrack, because there’s a Kardashian in the Ferrari garage. But we tend to get grumpy about such things and we digress…

entry.content:
1 minute read
GoPro Mission 1 close-up filters: price, specs
2:32

GoPro and PolarPro's Mission 1 diopters cost $49.99 for one or $99.99 for a set. The +2 cuts minimum focus to 30 cm (11.8 in).

GoPro has officially announced three new close-focus diopters, made by PolarPro from optical-grade multi-coated glass, for the Mission 1 series.

They were first flagged at the Mission 1 launch in May and address one of the range’s key weaknesses. While the new larger 1-in sensor in the cameras was welcomed by many, for a few users the fact that the close-focus distance suddenly increased to 60 cm (24 in) was a problem.

The new transparent filters slide over the camera lens or ND filter and use static focus, so no adjustment is required. A standalone +0.5 Close-Up Filter is pitched at vlog-style content, lifestyle footage, and travel shots, while a three-filter Close-Up Filter Set (+0.5, +1, and +2) is also available for more flexibility. As is usually the case with these filters, increasing diopter strength increases subject separation and gives a shallower depth of field.

Distance details

Focus distances are 50 cm (19.7 in) to 150 cm (59 in) for the standalone +0.5 filter, 45 cm (17.7 in) to 90 cm (35.4 in) for the +1, and 30 cm (11.8 in) to 50 cm (19.7 in) for the +2. For uses such as shooting in confined spaces like car interiors, where the 60 cm limit was a problem, the stronger filters bring subjects within reach, although each strength also caps how far away you can focus.

Users have to stack the diopters in front of ND filters rather than the other way around, though GoPro says that camera tracking in VLOG mode does not track subjects well when an ND filter and a diopter are stacked. It also notes that the far focus on the +0.5 is limited to 150 cm to create the subject separation and depth-of-field effect, and high-vibration activities and quick camera movements may affect video stabilization with the +2.

Pricing and availability

The standalone Close-Up Filter costs $49.99, while the Close-Up Filter Set costs $99.99. Both are available now globally at GoPro.com. They are compatible with the Mission 1 and Mission 1 PRO, as well as the Mission 1 PRO Grip Edition, Creator Edition, and Ultimate Creator Edition, and are backed by PolarPro’s Adventure Assurance.

entry.content:
3 minute read
Sigma FP2: price, specs, and release date
4:49

The Sigma FP2 costs $2199 body-only and arrives November 11. It has a 24.5-megapixel sensor, records 6K OpenGate, but the internal EVF rumors were wide of the mark.

Sigma’s much-anticipated FP2 L-Mount full-frame camera has been officially unveiled. It will be available on Wednesday, November 11, 2026 at authorized Sigma retailers starting at $2199 (body only). It will also be sold as a bundle with the 50mm F2 DG | Contemporary lens ($2749) or the Electronic Viewfinder EVF-21 ($2749).

That gives you a steer on the biggest rumor involving the camera not coming to pass. Back in early October, numerous sources (including us, mea culpa) stated confidently that the FP2 would integrate an EVF into the camera body. That hasn’t happened. On the plus side, neither has the rumored $2500 price point. Swings and roundabouts and all that.

Sigma claims the FP2 has the world’s smallest full-frame body and it certainly is small. It comes in at a meager 112.8 x 69.9 x 41.8 mm (4.4 x 2.8 x 1.6 in) and weighs 446 g (15.7 oz) including battery. Body only is an even more impressive 388 g (13.7 oz).

It packs plenty into that, however. The camera has a 24.5-megapixel partially stacked CMOS sensor with high-speed readout that reduces rolling shutter distortion. It shoots continuously at up to approximately 20 fps for up to 200 frames in a single burst. Subject detection recognizes people, animals, and birds, while thirteen color modes are selectable with a dedicated “Color” button.

Sigma's pitching this as a proper hybrid, one that strips down to a pocketable street camera or builds up into a full production rig with cine lenses, matte boxes, and wireless monitors.

Video-first

Speculation pre-release pegged the downgrading of the sensor (the fp L offered 61 MP) as signposting a tilt toward video, and a video-heavy feature set bears that out, though the lack of IBIS could be an issue.

A dedicated switch on top of the body toggles between STILL and CINE modes, each with its own functions, user interface, and workflow. In CINE mode, the FP2 offers 6K OpenGate recording and up to 14.1 stops of dynamic range (4K FF L-Log), with 7 stops of highlight headroom at ISO 1250 and above. It has 70 GB of internal storage in addition to an SD card slot, with recording continuing to internal storage when the memory card is full. The card could fill fairly quickly, since the camera supports ProRes RAW. It also supports L-Log from Leica Camera AG and 32-bit float audio (though that requires the optional HU-21 hot shoe unit with the Panasonic DMW-XLR2 and DMW-DMS1).

The Director’s Viewfinder function simulates the shooting ranges of various brands’ cinema cameras, including the ARRI ALEXA 35 and Sony VENICE 2 / BURANO. A desqueeze display mode is available for anamorphic lenses, while the optional LCD Viewfinder LVF-21 (sold separately) lets users check the view on the optical axis. This mounts over the LCD monitor, cuts out extraneous light, has diopter adjustment from −2 to +1 dpt, and magnifies the LCD 2.5x.

The tilting rear LCD tilts up 90° and down 45°. As to the additional EVF accessory, the EVF-21 attaches via a single USB-C port and tilts upward by up to 90°. Designed specifically for the FP2, it comes with a large eye cup, and features a 0.5-inch OLED panel with approximately 5.76 million dots. We don’t have figures for its weight, but the photo below shows just how much extra area it takes up on the side of the camera.

Stills-wise, native ISO runs 100 to 102,400 and expands down to ISO 6 for stills. The shutter runs 30 seconds to 1/25,600, plus bulb up to five minutes, with flash sync at 1/50s without a crop. Sigma says battery life is approximately 30% longer than the original fp, providing enough juice for approximately 370 still images or about 130 minutes of video.

Pricing and availability

We've covered this already, but for those that skip to the end to find this information, the FP2  will be available on November 11 starting at $2199 (body only). It will also be sold as a bundle with the (equally new) 50mm F2 DG | Contemporary lens at $274, or the Electronic Viewfinder EVF-21, which is also $2749.
